Commentary.Commentary: Right then, Sri Lanka have taken the lead in the series, and this win will certainly boost their confidence heading into the next game. As for Australia, while they will want to not dwell too much on this defeat, they will undoubtedly take valuable learnings as they continue their preparations for the Champions Trophy. The second and final game of the ODI series will take place here at the same venue on Friday, 14th February. It will be another day game, with the first ball set to be bowled at 4.30 am GMT. For now, you can switch tabs and catch the action from the other two ODI games on this blockbuster Wednesday. In Ahmedabad, riding on a century from Shubman Gill, India have posted 356 in the third ODI against England. Meanwhile, over in Karachi, South Africa are well-placed to post a daunting total against Pakistan in what is a virtual semi-final, with the winner set to take on New Zealand in the tri-series final. It's all shaping up to be an exciting day of cricket. See you there. Cheers!

The captain of Sri Lanka, Charith Asalanka is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his brilliant knock of 127 runs off 126 balls. He says that this was the best knock of his ODI career. Adds that he wanted to take the innings deep. Mentions that the way Dunith Wellalage started the innings, set the platform for him and a lot of credit should go to him. Shares that it was a tricky wicket to bat and he was confident at the halfway mark that his bowlers could defend this total. Further says that getting wickets early with the new ball was key and he is glad that they managed to do that.

Steven Smith, the captain of Australia thinks that the toss was not that important. Says that Charith Asalanka was the difference between the two teams, and appreciates him for batting really well. Mentions that their bowlers did a good job but the batters could not get going. Mentions the seamers getting that movement was good to see and also states that there was not much turn early on and the ball was skidding off the deck. On being asked about the Champions Trophy, he says they are keeping the big tournament in mind and preparing accordingly. Concludes by saying they were outplayed and will come back stronger in the second ODI.
Time for the presentation ceremony...

Dunith Wellalage is up for a quick chat. He says that this performance and win is special just because it came against an Aussie side. Adds that his teammates gave him support. Mentions that he had a chat with the coach Sanath Jayasuriya before going into bat and the message from him was to support the captain. Further mentions that the wicket was really good and he was trying to vary pace a bit. Concludes by saying that this win is the most memorable one so far in his ODI career.

Earlier in the game, after opting to bat, Sri Lanka were rocked early. The Aussie pacers made the most of the conditions, reducing the home side to 55/5, with the batters struggling with their footwork. Charith Asalanka and Dunith Wellalage rallied, but once that stand was broken, Charith was left fighting a lone battle. He found a solid ally in Eshan Malinga, who contributed just 1 in their 79-run stand but showed great defensive resilience. Asalanka's career-best ODI knock of 127 helped Sri Lanka recover, reaching 214 after being at a perilous 135/8.

For Sri Lanka, Asitha Fernando provided them with early inroads, but as expected, the Sri Lankan spinners took control during the middle phase. Maheesh Theekshana was the pick of the bowlers, finishing with figures of 4 for 40 in 9.5 overs, including a maiden. Dunith Wellalage chipped in with a couple of wickets to go with his 30-run knock earlier in the day. Wanindu Hasaranga struggled to get his radar right, much like his leg-spinner counterpart in Australia, Adam Zampa.

Australia endured a similarly tough start as Sri Lanka, with their batters not helping their cause through poor shot selection. Asitha Fernando did the early damage, and Maheesh Theekshana and Dunith Wellalage combined to leave the tourists reeling at 31/4. Alex Carey and Marnus Labuschagne then stitched together a recovery, with Carey taking the aggressive route. However, both Marnus and Carey fell in quick succession, leaving the lower order with too much to do. Aaron Hardie kept the flame of the chase alive, but once he perished, the fate was pretty much sealed.

Sri Lanka go 1-0 up with a fighting performance! Given their horror start at 55/5, not many would have backed them to come out victorious, let alone by a 49-run margin. However, Charith Asalanka’s heroic century gave them something to bowl at, and the bowlers followed up with a spirited display. As for Australia, they would have gladly accepted a target of 215 at the start of the day, but their lack of application and impatience at the crease proved costly. While the wicket did slow down in the second innings, batting was still very much possible with the right approach.

OUT! LBW! A huge shout for LBW, but not given by the umpire. Charith Asalanka signals the 'T' and takes the review to challenge the on-field decision. Maheesh Theekshana dishes out a fuller-length delivery, on middle and leg. It lands and then turns a shy bit into the batter, skidding through quickly. Spencer Johnson is a bit late to bring his bat through the line and misses as his bat hits the back pad. The ball goes on to clip his back pad. Ball Tracking shows that the ball is hitting the leg stump on the projection. Maheesh Theekshana finishes with a four-fer. SRI LANKA SUCCESSFULLY DEFEND THEIR TOTAL OF 214, AND WIN BY 49 RUNS!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! Sri Lanka will be pleased with this start, aided in part by some questionable shot selection from Australia’s top four. Since his arrival, Alex Carey has shown intent, while Marnus Labuschagne has looked to anchor the innings. The pitch has slowed down, with some deliveries keeping low, making batting a challenge. Sri Lanka still have plenty of spin options, with Wanindu Hasaranga yet to roll his arm over. How Australia navigate this spin test will likely dictate the course of the game. Just as we speak, here is he - Hasaranga into the attack.

Theekshana strikes in his very first over and Australia have been reduced to a worrisome 18/3. Maheesh Theekshana keeps bowling it flat and hits the fuller length, right in front of the stumps. It lands and skids through quickly off the deck. Cooper Connolly sits down on his knee to sweep it away but gets no wood on it and the ball raps him on the front pad. A huge, huge shout for LBW in unison from the Sri Lankans, and up goes the finger! Cooper Connolly chats with his skipper and decides to walk away without reviewing. Looked absolutely adjacent in real time and that's what Smith too would have thought. A disappointing outing with the bat for the young lad as he departs for 3 (16). Troubles looming large for the tourists now as the top three have been blown away within six overs.

Commentary.Commentary: Edged but it falls short! Just around the off stump line, on a good length, Jake Fraser-McGurk tries to hit on the up from the crease but the ball nips away to catch the outside edge. It drops short of the diving second slip fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Asitha Fernando to Jake Fraser-McGurk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR LEG BYES! Malinga slips onto the pads, on the fuller side, Cooper Connolly tries to help it away but misses. The ball brushes his pads and beats the diving keeper to his right for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Eshan Malinga to Cooper Connolly, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Hurls it on a back of a length, on off, Cooper Connolly stands tall to stab it down but the ball catches the inner half of the bat and rolls away in front of mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Eshan Malinga to Cooper Connolly, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a back of a length, on middle and leg, Jake Fraser-McGurk nudges it wide of mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Eshan Malinga to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bangs it in short on seeing the batter give him the charge, over off and middle, Jake Fraser-McGurk has a swing at it but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Eshan Malinga to Jake Fraser-McGurk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is on a hard length, on off, Jake Fraser-McGurk pats it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Eshan Malinga to Jake Fraser-McGurk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! At 129 kph, on a nagging length, outside off, Jake Fraser-McGurk takes a couple of steps down the track and has a swing across the line but connects nothing.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Eshan Malinga to Jake Fraser-McGurk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Eshan Malinga to operate from the far end.
Attacking the stumps, on a length, Jake Fraser-McGurk walks across his stumps and tucks it wide of mid on for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Asitha Fernando to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Almost chopped it back onto the stumps! On a good length, outside off, Cooper Connolly tries to force it through the off side and does not move his feet at all. The ball comes back in just enough to catch the inside edge and it sneaks past the stumps. It goes down to deep fine leg for a single. Cooper is underway as are Australia with this single!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Asitha Fernando to Cooper Connolly, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Very full, outside off, Cooper Connolly digs it out on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Asitha Fernando to Cooper Connolly, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Play and a miss! Asitha serves it fuller in length, around off, Cooper Connolly goes for the drive as he gets on the front foot but the ball nips back to cut him in half and beat him on the inside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Asitha Fernando to Cooper Connolly, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Out walks the 21-year-old Cooper Connolly at number 3.

OUT! A massive shout for LBW and the finger is raised! Matthew Short has a word with JFM and decides not to take the review. Sri Lanka have the early wicket they were after. Asitha lands it on a good length, on middle, Matthew Short looks to flick it away as the ball angles into him. It straightens after pitching and squares Short up. Goes past the outside edge and catches Short on the back pad. The height looked the most important factor there but the Ball Tracking shows that it would have turned out to be three reds with the ball crashing into the leg stump, so, a wise decision not to review but Australia lose Short for a duck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Asitha Fernando to Matthew Short, OUT! lbw b Asitha Fernando.

Commentary.Commentary: Beats the bat straight away! Bangs it on a hard length from over the wicket, Matthew Short tries to stand and deliver off the back foot but the ball does not rise as much as he expected it to. Goes under the bat on its way to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Asitha Fernando to Matthew Short, No run.
